paragraphs: Rav Adda bar Mattanah. Shabbat 107b: “Adda b.M.” should read Rav Adda. He asked Abaye there, 48a, and called Abaye “master,” Ketubbot 77b. He said Rava’s knife was sharp, Chullin 77a. Chapter Mi Shemeto: the first Ravina was his colleague in Rava’s time. In my view this is incorrect: Rav Adda bar Mattanah sat before Rava and objected to him, so was Rava’s student. The later Ravina was likewise Rava’s student (see there and my introductory rules), hence he was the later Ravina’s colleague; both questioned Rava. Rav Yosef, Rava’s teacher, answered the early Ravina’s words (see there), and Rav Adda bar Mattanah spoke with Rav Yosef. The Ravina answered by Rav Yosef is not Rav Ashi’s colleague. Thus Rav Adda bar Mattanah was the early Ravina’s student and later Ravina’s colleague. Yuchasin intends the passage there, 23: may one enter a fixed privy wearing tefillin to urinate? Ravina permitted, Rav Adda bar Mattanah forbade. They asked Rava, who forbade. End quotation. Seeing their dispute, he called them colleagues, but forgot Shevuot 18a: Rava told Rav Adda bar Mattanah, “Obey what your teacher Ravina tells you”; likewise Zevachim 100b, see Rashi. Thus Ravina was his teacher. He sat before Rava, Ketubbot 28a, 85a; Gittin 28b. He and Ravina asked Rava, Megillah 28b. He objected to Rava, Shabbat 8a; Eruvin 8, end of b, 34b. He said in Rav’s name, Shabbat 109b; Avodah Zarah 28, beginning of a. Perhaps this made She'erit Yosef count him among Rav’s students; see his error, for he was Rava’s student. He said in Rabbah’s name, beginning of chapter א״ע [title unresolved]. He told Rav Yosef, “You told us expressly.” Rav Nachman and Rav Sheshet sat, with him among them, discussing; he spoke to them, Zevachim 5b. He did not have compassion on his children and went to study Torah, Eruvin 22a. He was Othniel’s reincarnation (see part I, year 2516), his wife Achsah; they were poor for that repair (G.N., letter alef).
